title: balance.json health block uses jint: out-of-i32-range integers wrap and decimals truncate, bypassing the fail-fast validation
evidence:
b.health.window_ticks = jint(hobj, "window_ticks", -1)
b.health.exit_margin_pct = jint(hobj, "exit_margin_pct", -1)
b.health.exit_margin_ms = jint(hobj, "exit_margin_ms", -1)
b.health.drain_cap_pct_per_tick = jint(hobj, "drain_cap_pct_per_tick", -1)
b.health.recharge_pct_per_tick = jint(hobj, "recharge_pct_per_tick", -1)
b.health.win_uptime_pct = jint(hobj, "win_uptime_pct", -1)
b.health.grace_refill_per_tick = jint(hobj, "grace_refill_per_tick", -1)
b.health.grace_refill_streak_ticks = jint(hobj, "grace_refill_streak_ticks", -1)
---
case json.Integer: return i32(x)
case json.Float:   return i32(x)
detail: jint casts without range check: "window_ticks": 4294967496 wraps to 200 and passes 1..10000; "drain_cap_pct_per_tick": 4294967297 wraps to 1. Decimals (200.9) silently truncate. The new fail-fast validation is bypassed.
recommended_fix: Use jint_strict (range-checked, float-rejecting) for all eight health keys, like the packet_types health fields, and reject instead of wrapping.

title: surge_done is never reset when a new surge starts — a stale latch plus reset accumulators can fire Run_Won mid-second-surge on partial-window data
detail: After a below-threshold first window, surge_done stays latched. A second crisis-archetype set-piece resets accumulators to 0 while the gate stays open; the first delivery tick reads 100% uptime and wins mid-surge — a fake win E24 does not cover.
recommended_fix: Reset h.surge_done = false in the new-surge-start branch, so the ratio is only evaluated at each window's deactivation edge.

title: recharge_pct_per_tick == 0 (validation allows >= 0) emits an unchanged Meter_Changed event every healthy tick forever
detail: With recharge 0 and a meter below 100 (after any partial drain), the else-branch adds 0 and unconditionally appends Meter_Changed with the same value every tick — no-op event spam in every hash.
recommended_fix: Only emit Meter_Changed when the meter value actually changed (guard on recharge > 0 before the emit), or require recharge >= 1 at load.

title: A class with health_drain_pct_per_tick == 0 (validation allows >= 0) expires its grace but Grace_Expired is never emitted — emission is gated on drain > 0
detail: Severity 0 makes drain 0, so the expired list is discarded and Grace_Expired never lands: the event stream shows Grace_Started with no expiry, and the class silently never drains. Contract says expiry emits Grace_Expired.
recommended_fix: Emit the pending Grace_Expired events whenever the expired list is non-empty, independent of the drain amount, or reject a 0 severity at load.

title: The absent-when-disabled serialization contract (no health bytes when off) is claimed but never asserted — dump_off is deleted without a single check
detail: Test header claims pin (a) 'the health section is ABSENT when disabled' — the golden-stability rule — but no assertion touches dump_off; the rule is unpinned and can regress silently.
recommended_fix: Assert the disabled dump contains no health marker bytes (e.g. scan for the meter u32 + grace row pattern and expect not-found) before delete(dump_off).

title: The E30 exit-hysteresis band (tolerance - margin) is never actually asserted — the band test contains a tautological expectation
evidence:
testing.expectf(t, s.health.grace[0].grace_left > 0 || s.health.grace[0].grace_left == 0,
		"grace cell present for email")
detail: The test's own comment admits the band is 'pinned by test_health_windowed_breach_recovers' slide' — that test only shows exit below the margin, never that a ratio inside (27, 30] stays latched. Enter is pinned; the exit threshold is not.
recommended_fix: Add a fixture stepping a ratio into the band (e.g. 28%) and assert breach stays set, then below the margin and assert it clears.
